author: Genesis Apprentice Engine
description: Core conceptual vocabulary extracted from Fabio Valentini's discretionary Order Flow trading methodology. Concepts are organized by category and linked via semantic relationships.

categories.Market_State: The current condition of the market — the first question Fabio asks before any trade.
categories.Level: Price locations that matter, derived from Volume Profile and Market Structure.
categories.Order_Flow: Microstructural evidence of buyer/seller behavior at the footprint level.
categories.Setup: Specific trade configurations that emerge when State + Level + Flow align.
categories.Risk_Management: How Fabio protects capital and manages open positions.
categories.Session: Time-of-day context that influences volatility and directional bias.
categories.Price_Action: Observable price behavior that provides context or confirmation.
categories.Market_Structure: Macro structural elements that define the auction environment.

concepts.name: Balance
concepts.definition: Market is rotating around fair value, accepting price within a defined range. ~70% of the time. Do NOT trade breakouts here.

concepts.name: Imbalance
concepts.definition: One side is aggressively pushing price to discover new value. Characterized by displacement, momentum, and directional conviction.
visual_markers: price moving away from POC with volume

concepts.name: Compression
concepts.definition: Price is coiling into a tight range, building energy before an expansion move. Often precedes a breakout.

concepts.name: Opening_Drive
concepts.definition: The initial directional move after market open (especially NY 9:30). Sets the tone and bias for the session.

concepts.name: POC
concepts.definition: Point of Control — the price level with the highest traded volume. Represents fair value and the strongest magnet for price.
visual_markers: thickest horizontal line on volume profile

concepts.name: VAH
concepts.definition: Value Area High — the upper boundary of the 70% volume zone. Acts as resistance in balance; breakout target in imbalance.
visual_markers: upper line of value area rectangle

concepts.name: VAL
concepts.definition: Value Area Low — the lower boundary of the 70% volume zone. Acts as support in balance; breakdown target in imbalance.
visual_markers: lower line of value area rectangle

concepts.name: LVN
concepts.definition: Low Volume Node — a thinly traded area in the profile where price moves quickly. Key for entries in trend continuation.
visual_markers: gap or thin section in volume profile

concepts.name: HVN
concepts.definition: High Volume Node — a thick volume area where price tends to stall or reverse. Acts as support/resistance.

concepts.name: VWAP
concepts.definition: Volume Weighted Average Price — institutional benchmark. Above VWAP = bullish bias; below = bearish bias.

concepts.name: Value_Area
concepts.definition: The 70% of volume traded closest to the POC. Defines the accepted range of fair value for the session or structure.
visual_markers: rectangle on profile between VAH and VAL

concepts.name: Previous_Session_High_Low
concepts.definition: The high and low of the prior trading session. Often acts as key support/resistance and targets.
visual_markers: horizontal line at prior day extreme

concepts.name: Absorption
concepts.definition: Heavy volume at a level without price continuation. One side is absorbing the other's aggression, often signaling exhaustion and impending reversal.

concepts.name: Aggression
concepts.definition: One side is actively and forcefully pushing price. Seen in large footprint bubbles, stacked imbalances, and CVD divergence.

concepts.name: Delta
concepts.definition: The net difference between buying and selling pressure at each price level. Positive delta = buyers aggressive; negative = sellers aggressive.

concepts.name: CVD
concepts.definition: Cumulative Volume Delta — the running total of delta. Shows which side has been in control over time. Trending CVD = sustained aggression.
visual_markers: CVD line trending up or down

concepts.name: Footprint
concepts.definition: The ATAS footprint chart showing bid/ask volume at each price level. Reveals microstructure: absorption, aggression, and imbalance.

concepts.name: Stacked_Imbalance
concepts.definition: Multiple consecutive price levels showing the same directional imbalance (e.g., 3+ levels of buying). Signals strong aggression.
visual_markers: 3+ consecutive cells colored same direction on footprint

concepts.name: Exhaustion
concepts.definition: The aggressive side is running out of orders. Seen as delta divergence, shrinking volume on new highs/lows, and absorption.
visual_markers: price makes new high but delta lower

concepts.name: NASDAQ_Effort
concepts.definition: Fabio's proprietary term for aggressive footprint clusters showing institutional effort at key levels. Used to confirm entries and management points.

concepts.name: Failed_Auction
concepts.definition: Price tests a key level multiple times but fails to break through. Indicates absorption and often leads to a reversal or mean reversion.

concepts.name: Triple_A_Setup
concepts.definition: Fabio's highest conviction setup requiring three aligned elements: Absorption + Accumulation + Aggression at a key level.

concepts.name: Trend_Continuation
concepts.definition: Entering in the direction of the established trend after a pullback to a key level (often LVN or prior balance level).

concepts.name: Mean_Reversion
concepts.definition: Trading back toward POC or balance center after a failed breakout or rejection at the edge of value. Best in balance or compressed markets.
visual_markers: price breaks out then reclaims back inside

concepts.name: Opening_Range_Breakout
concepts.definition: Trading the breakout of the first 15-30 minute range after NY open. Requires aggression and volume confirmation.

concepts.name: Value_Area_Bounce
concepts.definition: Price tests VAH or VAL and bounces back into the value area. Requires order flow confirmation (absorption or aggression reversal).

concepts.name: Squeeze
concepts.definition: A rapid acceleration move after compression. Price breaks out of a tight range with explosive momentum.

concepts.name: False_Breakout
concepts.definition: Price briefly breaks a key level then immediately reverses. Traps breakout traders. High-probability mean reversion signal.

concepts.name: Stop_Loss_in_Profit
concepts.definition: Moving the stop loss to breakeven or into profit after price has moved favorably. Fabio's primary management technique.
visual_markers: stop now at entry or better

concepts.name: Risk_to_Reward
concepts.definition: The ratio of potential profit to initial risk. Fabio targets minimum 1:3, often 1:5 or higher on NASDAQ.
visual_markers: entry, stop, and target lines on chart

concepts.name: Daily_Loss_Limit
concepts.definition: Fabio stops trading after 3 losses or a defined daily drawdown. Preserves capital and mental state.

concepts.name: Trailing_Stop
concepts.definition: Moving the stop loss progressively higher/lower as price moves favorably. Used only on exceptional trend days.

concepts.name: Position_Size
concepts.definition: The number of contracts traded. Fabio scales size based on conviction and volatility. NASDAQ = fewer contracts due to volatility.

concepts.name: Mismanagement
concepts.definition: When Fabio holds a position too long, ignores absorption, or fails to take profit at target. He explicitly reviews these errors.
visual_markers: trade going from profit to loss

concepts.name: NY_Session
concepts.definition: New York trading session, 9:30 AM - 4:00 PM EST. Highest volatility and liquidity. Fabio's primary trading window.

concepts.name: London_Session
concepts.definition: London trading session, ~3:00 AM - 11:00 AM EST. Often more balanced and mean-reverting. Fabio trades mean reversion here.

concepts.name: Pre_Market
concepts.definition: Trading before NY open. Lower liquidity. Fabio uses pre-market structure to plan NY open scenarios.

concepts.name: Market_Close
concepts.definition: End of trading session. Fabio often closes before close to avoid volatility decay and slippage.

concepts.name: Breakout
concepts.definition: Price moves decisively beyond a key level (VAH, VAL, range high/low) with volume and aggression.

concepts.name: Pullback
concepts.definition: A temporary counter-trend move after an impulse. Fabio uses pullbacks to enter in the trend direction at better prices.

concepts.name: Reversal
concepts.definition: A change in direction after a trend or test. Often preceded by absorption, failed auction, or exhaustion.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.definition: A strong, impulsive move with little retracement. Indicates imbalance and institutional participation.

concepts.name: Gap
concepts.definition: A price discontinuity between close and next open. Fabio notes gaps and often waits for them to fill before managing.

concepts.name: Reclaim
concepts.definition: Price breaks a level but then moves back through it in the opposite direction. Key signal for false breakout/mean reversion.
visual_markers: wick beyond level then close back inside

concepts.name: Slippage
concepts.definition: The difference between expected fill price and actual fill. Common in fast markets, especially at NASDAQ close.
visual_markers: order fill price worse than stop
P&L showing larger loss than expected

concepts.name: Higher_High
concepts.definition: Price makes a new high above the previous swing high. Bullish structural development.

concepts.name: Lower_Low
concepts.definition: Price makes a new low below the previous swing low. Bearish structural development.

concepts.name: Bias
concepts.definition: The directional inclination based on structure, fundamentals, and session context. Fabio establishes bias before looking for setups.

concepts.name: Volatility
concepts.definition: The degree of price movement. Fabio distinguishes between directional volatility (tradeable) and choppy volatility (avoid).

concepts.name: Liquidation
concepts.definition: A forced position closure, usually via stop loss. Fabio shows these as learning moments.

concepts.name: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: Macro context (economic reports, news, data) that informs Fabio's directional bias for the session.

concepts.name: Direction
concepts.definition: The prevailing price trajectory — up, down, or sideways. Fabio establishes directional bias before any setup.

concepts.name: Discipline
concepts.definition: The mental rigor to follow rules, respect limits, and avoid emotional trading decisions.

concepts.name: Entry
concepts.definition: The specific price and moment where a position is initiated. Must align with State + Level + Flow.
visual_markers: price at key level with confirmation

concepts.name: Expansion
concepts.definition: A widening of the trading range after compression. Price breaks out of a tight coil with increased volatility.

concepts.name: Explosion
concepts.definition: A sudden, violent price move after a period of compression or balance. Often triggered by news or order flow climax.

concepts.name: Higher_Low
concepts.definition: A pullback low that holds above the previous swing low. Bullish structural confirmation.

concepts.name: Lower_High
concepts.definition: A rally high that fails below the previous swing high. Bearish structural confirmation.

concepts.name: Market_State
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for all market condition classifications. The first question Fabio answers.

concepts.name: Market_Structure
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for macro structural elements that define the auction environment.

concepts.name: Momentum
concepts.definition: The rate and strength of price movement. Sustained momentum confirms directional conviction.

concepts.name: Neutral
concepts.definition: No directional bias. Market is unclear or balanced. Fabio often stays flat until bias resolves.

concepts.name: Order_Flow
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for microstructural evidence of buyer and seller behavior at the footprint level.

concepts.name: Price
concepts.definition: The current market price. The central variable that all analysis revolves around.

concepts.name: Profit_Target
concepts.definition: The price level where a winning position is closed for profit. Defined before entry based on structure.

concepts.name: Psychology
concepts.definition: The mental and emotional state of the trader. Fabio emphasizes that psychology is as important as technicals.

concepts.name: Reflection
concepts.definition: Post-trade review and learning. Fabio explicitly reflects on errors, mismanagement, and lessons after each session.

concepts.name: Retracement
concepts.definition: A temporary price move against the prevailing trend. Synonymous with pullback in Fabio's vocabulary.

concepts.name: Revenge_Trading
concepts.definition: Trading impulsively after a loss to recover money. Fabio explicitly warns against this destructive behavior.

concepts.name: Setup
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for specific trade configurations that emerge when State + Level + Flow align.

concepts.name: Stop_Loss
concepts.definition: The predefined price level where a losing position is closed to limit risk. The maximum acceptable loss per trade.

concepts.name: Target
concepts.definition: The intended exit price for a profitable trade. Synonymous with profit target in Fabio's methodology.

concepts.name: Technical_Only
concepts.definition: Trading purely on technical analysis without considering fundamentals. Fabio sometimes contrasts this with fundamental-informed bias.

concepts.name: Trade_Management
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for all position and risk management activities — entries, stops, targets, sizing, and psychological control.

concepts.name: Volume_Profile
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for volume-based price analysis. The distribution of traded volume across price levels.

concepts.name: Exit
concepts.definition: Closing a position, either at target, stop, or discretionary management point.

concepts.name: Impulse
concepts.definition: A strong directional price move with little to no retracement. The 'trend' part of trend + pullback structure.

concepts.name: Level
concepts.definition: Abstract root concept for any price location that matters in the market structure. Levels are derived from volume profile, market structure, and prior session data.
